units.translation: The aorist has one passive form ἠχθέσθην [I was grieved].
Beware of this, lest his heart ever be grieved.
The burden of the present evil will always wear you down.
[ἄχθεα [burdens] wrongly for ἄχεα [griefs] Ch. 419. Hermann reads ἀχθέων [of burdens] for ἀχέων [of griefs] Sept. 949, on which see under διόσδοτος [given by Zeus].]
A burden not easy to embrace.
If the vain burden of care must truly be cast off.
Or a storm, a common burden, seized the army.
The burden doubles the disease for the one who possesses it.
And this blood-dripping burden would be borne for the house.
And may it be an ever-living burden to the land.
For some Stygian darkness hovers over.
And a dark mist is spoken of throughout the house by a much-groaning report.
ἄχνη [foam, spray]. But Aeschylus (fr. 364) uses it for smoke.
in a verse, as it seems, of an interpolator
What is this new great grief?
By what man is this grief (Auratus reads ἄγος [pollution]) being prepared?
He tore away (this is corrupt) the grief.
And with god-hated grief the race of mortals, dishonored, is gone.
Do not lament the present griefs.
Of griefs — these things from near at hand.
Of Zeus-given griefs (Hermann reads ἀχθέων [of burdens]).
Shall I cry aloud the all-wretched griefs?
These are the griefs in the house at the hearth.
To the swift-passing ferry of griefs.
That the gods, avengers of mortals, watch over griefs (Auratus reads ἄγη [pollutions]) from above the earth.
Most glorious, he accomplished of griefs.
Monthly griefs (thus I corrected for μηνεῖται ἄκη [he rages, remedies]).
The griefs which we suffered (thus Blomfield for χθες [yesterday]) at the hands of our parents.
For the earth nourishes many terrible griefs of fears.
Cry out and shout things more bitter than griefs.
So that you may hear new things and fresh griefs.
Nor to shine a light for the poor.
Lord Apollo, a prophet truthful before.
You have spoken a truthful word about the order.
The divine, truthful mouth of Phoebus.
For examples from Homer and the tragedians see Thes. vol. 1, 2 p. 2785.
Having completed a long length of time, you will come back to the light.
For fear seizes the tongue through faint-heartedness.
To fawn upon death and battle through faint-heartedness.
You have destroyed the lifeless cowardice.
done in the dead of night
done in the dead of night
A cry in the dead of night.
And in that night the god stirred up an untimely storm.
And I forbid the untimely fates that slay men.
[Dobree's conjecture Suppl. 963 for λωτίσασθε [pluck the flower]. See λωτίζομαι [I pluck the flower].]
Nor may Ares, the mortal-destroying bedfellow of Aphrodite, cut off the flower.
